description: Hi! I'm Dennis, a high-energy builder who loves coding and product design.Our challenge is to find places on Earth that match the conditions of Mars.
summary:
Twin Shores is a ranking system that finds lakes on Earth most similar to Jezero Crater, the dry lake bed on Mars where Perseverance is searching for signs of ancient life. We scored 70 places on eight variables: 38 lakes in Türkiye, 24 lakes from other countries, and 8 known Mars analog sites such as the Atacama Desert. Four variables come from NASA and ESA data (temperature, air pressure, evaporation, terrain slope) and four from published studies (water pH, carbonate minerals, lake type, sediments).

This addresses the challenge by turning “which place on Earth is like Mars?” into a measurable, comparable score. To check that our own weighting choices didn’t drive the result, we re-ran the ranking with 5,000 random weightings. Lake Salda, the lake NASA already pairs with Jezero, ranked first and stayed first in 69% of them. Lake Van in Türkiye and Lake Alchichica in Mexico came next.

This matters because mission teams rehearse sampling and test instruments at places like these before they fly. Knowing which sites match, and how well, helps them choose where to practice.
details:
What it does. Twin Shores ranks places on Earth by how closely they match Jezero Crater and shows why. Pick a lake on the map and you get its score, every variable next to Jezero's value, and the study behind each finding. A Lake Salda page puts it beside Jezero: both seen from orbit, the shape of both basins, the evidence side by side, and a field-test plan. A 3D view lets you drive a rover over the real terrain of Salda, Van and Erçek, and Jezero, with a minimap. One button fills Jezero with its ancient lake; another lowers Lake Salda to show what a shrinking lake would expose. Both are labelled as simulations.

How it works. We started from all 148 natural lakes in Türkiye listed on Wikidata. We kept the 38 that have published evidence or lie within 150 km of Lake Salda, and added 24 lakes from other countries: carbonate and microbialite lakes, soda lakes, impact-crater lakes, and five large lakes we expected to match poorly, as a check. Known analogs such as the Atacama Desert, Death Valley and Haughton Crater are in the list too. For each place, Python scripts read temperature, air pressure and evaporation from NASA POWER, and terrain slope from the NASA/METI ASTER elevation model. Jezero's slope comes from NASA's MOLA data on the same 900 m grid. Water pH, minerals, lake type and sediments have no global dataset, so we entered a match from 0 to 1 for each, with the study it came from. A place's score is the weighted average of the variables it has, and every score says how many variables it rests on.

What we found. Lake Salda scores 0.741 on seven of eight variables: alkaline water (pH 9.1 to 9.5), a white hydromagnesite shore, microbialites and a closed basin. Lake Van (0.693) is a soda lake with carbonate towers up to 40 m tall. Lake Alchichica in Mexico (0.689) is a crater lake whose microbialites are also made of hydromagnesite. Lake Erçek (0.687), beside Van, is a little-studied soda lake. We tested the ranking three ways. With the weights redrawn at random 5,000 times, Salda stays in the top three 94% of the time. Dropping any one variable keeps Salda, Van and Erçek in the top five. Slope measured again with Copernicus EU-DEM agrees with ASTER at r = 0.99.

Limits. No place on Earth has Mars's thin air, cold or radiation, so our sites match Jezero's ancient lake, not Mars today. Jezero's lake has no measured pH. Places are scored on different numbers of variables. On climate and slope alone, Salda falls to 31st of 70 and the Atacama to 61st; the match comes from chemistry and rocks. The list of places is a choice, and changing it shifts every score a little. We covered Mars only.

Benefits and aims. The method is open and repeatable. Anyone can add lakes, targets or variables by editing one file and rerunning the scripts. We would like a field team to sample Lake Erçek's shore for carbonates and to compare Salda and Alchichica directly.

Tools. Python 3 for the data pipeline. HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the website, with Leaflet for maps and three.js for 3D. Data from NASA POWER, ASTER GDEM, MOLA, SRTM and Mars Trek, Copernicus EU-DEM and Sentinel-2, and Wikidata. Hosted on GitHub Pages. AI tools as listed in section 6.
